title: Traffic Curve Conductor — wireflow & rollback rehearsal
creator: Amelia Park
description:
Objective: Design a compact, expressive composer for staged traffic shifts that lets engineers and PMs author non-linear traffic curves, preview their runtime effects, and rehearse rollbacks. The 'Traffic Curve Conductor' is a canvas + timeline hybrid: users draw or select a baseline distribution, apply named segments (canary, cohort A/B, experiment shadow), and define safety constraints (latency, error rate, user-impact thresholds). The composer produces a machine-readable plan that maps to rollout policies (percentages, duration, gating signals) and a live rehearsal mode that simulates traffic movement against historical telemetry.

Scope: mid-fidelity wireflow and interactive prototype for the Console's Rollouts tab. Includes: 1) Composer canvas with curve drawing, easing presets, and drag handles for segment boundaries; 2) Timeline panel with phase metadata (duration, target percent, gating conditions); 3) Confidence band overlay showing expected latency/cost delta per phase; 4) Rehearsal mode that plays forward using canned telemetry and records potential policy breaches; 5) Quick-rollback choreographer — a one-click escalation that creates an emergency rollback plan and a shallow approval flow.

Design goals and constraints: keep primary actions visible in 1 row for fast PLG usage; make the safety state explicit (green/amber/red) with textual hints for non-engineers; preserve compatibility with Dedicated/Private routing policies (we only expose compatible model variants); show token-cost delta and latency delta per staged step. The composer must map cleanly to runtime config (rollout.duration, target_percent, gating.signal, fallback.model_variant) to avoid translation errors during implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive prototype demonstrates creating a 3-phase rollout and editing target percentages via curve handles
Timeline panel lists phase metadata and updates in real time when curve is edited
Rehearsal mode shows simulated latency and cost overlays and flags policy breaches
Quick-rollback flow creates a rollback plan pre-populated with previous stable variant and exposes confirm/notify actions
Design tokens and spacing conform to Console 2.0 standards; a11y contrast checks pass for primary controls
recent_activity: 2026-02-21 — Initial whiteboard: three interaction approaches (draw-nudge, percent-grid, staged-rows). Chose draw-nudge as primary for discoverability.
2026-02-26 — Mid-fidelity screens uploaded. Added confidence-band overlay after research call with SRE (shows 90% latency band computed from sample telemetry).

2026-03-03 — Design review with PM (Jules Tan) + Eng (Maya Chen). PM requests explicit token-cost delta per phase; Eng requests JSON mapping for rollout.duration & gating.signal. Action: add code snippet export and token delta row.
2026-03-07 — Accessibility pass: increased contrast on timeline separators and added keyboard-only handles for phase focus.
2026-03-10 — Usability session with three platform engineers: shorthand for creating emergency rollback praised, but they requested an undo stack with timestamped checkpoints. Added to next steps.
notes_and_feedback: PM (Jules Tan): 'We need to make it impossible to publish a plan that violates active dedicated capacity constraints' — requires upstream capacity check API (ENG dependency).
SRE (Olivia Park): 'Confidence band should be plottable per-region; assume regional telemetry differences.'
Design lead (Kunal Rao): 'Consider a compact 'chart-only' embed for dashboards where rollouts are monitored post-publish.'
Engineering (Maya Chen): 'Export must include a strict schema and a dry-run endpoint mapping; add a preview JSON panel for advanced users.'

Should quick-rollback auto-notify on-call or only create a changelist? (policy decision)
How to represent branching experiments (A/B with nested canaries) in the curve composer? — placeholder UX needed
